To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) farmers' observations of crop response to management are of little use to other farmers, unless they describe the circumstances under which these observations were made; (2) the value of information obtained through farmers' experiences and experiments is enhanced when these circumstances are characterized within a recommendation domain; (3) the definition of HE as recommendation domains at the farm scale is valid; (4) the effectiveness of distinct practices for specific HEs can be identified with appropriate methodologies.

The definition of HEs (homologous events) as recommendation domains at the farm scale is valid, and the effectiveness of distinct crop management practices for specific HEs can be identified with a multi-stage analytic procedure that combines expert guidance, conditional forests and mixed models."

farmers' observations are useful for the development of recommendation domains, and that the use of these domains for data analysis increases the power of the analysis and the usefulness of the resulting information.
The main takeaway from our work is that

farmers are capable of observing and responding to the conditions under which they farm, and that their observations can be used to develop management recommendations that are adapted to the specific circumstances of their fields.
the definition of recommendation domains is possible at the farm scale, and the identification of management practices effective for distinct domains is feasible.
the value of data from on-farm experiments and farmer observations is enhanced when the data are analyzed within the context of recommendation domains.
